For each one, give me the number, description, priority and scheduled date, and say whether it needs the unit de-energized, for example internal inspection, OLTC work or electrical testing, or whether it can be done live, for example oil sampling. Group the outage-needing work orders into bundles. Each bundle must have at least two work orders whose scheduled dates fall within 14 days of each other. For each bundle, propose a single outage date where the MAIN calendar has the fewest other scheduled work orders. Estimate each bundle's total planned hours, using the planned hours on the work orders themselves. Where a work order has no plan, use the average actual hours of closed work orders on Transformer 1. Then check the latest acetylene and hydrogen. If acetylene is above 1 ppm, any bundle with OLTC or inspection work moves to the earliest possible date regardless of calendar load. If fewer than two outage-needing work orders exist, don't bundle anything. Recommend whether each one should be done alone or deferred to the next planned outage, and why.

One matching work order exists; it is awaiting approval.

| Number | Description | Priority | Scheduled date | De-energization needed? |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1000051 | Transformer 1 — 2-day outage and inspection (including OLTC) | 1 | Not scheduled | **Yes:** transformer/OLTC inspection requires isolation. |

**No bundles:** only one outage-needing work order exists. No live-capable work orders were found.

### Recommendation
**Do 1000051 alone at the earliest operationally feasible outage rather than defer.** Obtain approval and coordinate safe isolation, crew availability and manufacturer support.

Latest available readings, both dated **2024-01-19 UTC**:
- **Acetylene: 7 ppm**, above your 1 ppm threshold.
- **Hydrogen: 2,850 ppm**.

These readings support prioritizing inspection, but they are historical—not evidence of today’s condition. Obtain fresh DGA urgently and revalidate the outage timing. The January 2024 outage dates in the notes are historical proposals, not scheduled dates.

**Hours cannot be estimated using your rule:** this work order has no planned labor hours, and no closed Transformer 1 work orders exist to calculate an actual-hours average. Its “2-day outage” description is not a labor-hours plan.

No scheduling changes were made.
